Definition: from G5259 and G2192; to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience:--suffer.
BiblicalUsage: hypéchō means to hold under, to endure with patience. In Jude 1:7, the text says "suffering the vengeance of eternal fire."
TheologicalSignificance: I read hypéchō plainly — it means to hold under, to endure with patience, and I do not build a doctrine on it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
